$conventions: Each block's `role` is looked up in the live DOM via [data-kind="<role>"] (the codebase's own component-root convention). A height/y/x/width field valued the literal string "content" is content-driven (depends on real project count/copy/media) and is always skipped, never a defect — see template-check.mjs's header comment.

gridChecks only apply to Desktop (D) templates: the site's own CSS gates the 12-col grid behind the `lg` breakpoint (`lg:grid-cols-12` / `.layout-grid-grid[data-columns]`); Mobile (M) layouts are single-column, so a grid-snap check there would be meaningless.
A field simply omitted (not present on the block) is not checked at all — used where the DS inventory gave no number to check against, to avoid asserting a value that was never actually sourced.

OPINION GRADIENT (design-system-opinion-gradient.md, ratified 2026-07-29): a TEMPLATE is a page layout — the highest level, ALL the opinion (which blocks, in what order, with which props/overrides). The Example frame's RESOLVED INSTANCE STATE (after every override) IS this spec — an override is the layout exercising its rightful opinion, never drift to reconcile away.

AXIS OWNERSHIP: `device` is the one axis a block owns (its own internal adaptation, e.g. NavigationHeader always renders both its top bar and its mobile-nav pill in the DOM, CSS just breakpoint-hides one — see navigation-header.tsx). Every other axis belongs to the layout, ONE opinion per axis, so a template's D-/M- pair is one layout opinion rendered twice. `deviceOnly: true` on a block marks it as that block's own device chrome (excluded from the D/M sequence comparison); a role present on both sides that isn't deviceOnly must carry identical non-geometry props (styleProbes, spacer state) — device explains geometry differences (heights/positions), never a style/props divergence.

SPACERS: a block's outer spacerTop/spacerBottom is authored layout opinion (zero-opinion component default is OFF — token-rulings.md 'Blocks carry OUTER spacers; default spacer-top = FALSE', 2026-07-29). Declare `spacerTop`/`spacerBottom` on a block entry only where verified against the real call site (page.tsx); omitted means unchecked, same as any other field.

NAVIGATIONHEADER FILL: its Figma fill is bound-but-unused (capability-present-unused, token-rulings.md 2026-07-29) — code renders no background anywhere, so the computed background-color probe expects "transparent" universally. This is NOT the Figma-side invisible-fill capability seed showing through as a code bug; never 'fix' it by asserting a real color.

styleProbes.$note: NavigationHeader's fill is bound-but-unused in Figma (capability-present-unused, token-rulings.md 2026-07-29) — code renders NO background on every route, not just Home's overlay pages. This probe holds on every template that checks navigation-header, mirrored on M-Home per the device-pairing rule (design-system-opinion-gradient.md): background-color isn't a device axis, so the D/M pair must carry the identical opinion.

Mirrors D-Home's probe — see D-Home's $note. Device-pairing check (design-system-opinion-gradient.md) flagged this as missing before the fix; background-color isn't a device axis so the pair must match.

M-Projects.$note: The inventory doc has no dedicated M-Projects section (only D-Projects was captured). hero-text is added here anyway (568/tall, not content-driven) because it's sourced by inference, not invention: Projects passes HeroText the identical height=medium/heightLg=tall/hasDescription=false props as Home (verified against projects/page.tsx and page.tsx), so it resolves to the same mobile height M-Home's own hero-text entry asserts — the device-pairing check (design-system-opinion-gradient.md) flagged its total absence as a sequence mismatch device can't explain. layout-grid stays omitted: no sourced mobile grid/card numbers exist, and its D-side entry is content-driven (height: 'content'), which the pairing check exempts from requiring a mirrored M entry.
